## Purpose

`earthquakes` provides tools to **clean**, **visualize** and **map** the NOAA
Significant Earthquake Database. The data are messy in a few ways that this
package fixes: the date is split in three columns, the coordinates can be read as
text, and the location names carry the country in capital letters.

```{r load}
library(earthquakes)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

file <- system.file("extdata", "earthquakes.tsv.gz", package = "earthquakes")
raw <- readr::read_delim(file, delim = "\t", show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(raw)
```

## Cleaning: `eq_clean_data()` and `eq_location_clean()`

`eq_clean_data()` adds a `DATE` column (class `Date`) and makes `LATITUDE` and
`LONGITUDE` numeric. `eq_location_clean()` drops the country from
`LOCATION_NAME` and uses title case.

```{r clean}
clean <- raw %>% eq_clean_data() %>% eq_location_clean()
clean %>%
  filter(COUNTRY == "MEXICO", lubridate::year(DATE) >= 2000) %>%
  select(DATE, LOCATION_NAME, EQ_PRIMARY, TOTAL_DEATHS) %>%
  head()
```

## Time line: `geom_timeline()` and `geom_timeline_label()`

`geom_timeline()` draws one point per earthquake along a time line. Map the
magnitude to `size` and the number of deaths to `colour`. A factor mapped to `y`
gives one time line per level.

```{r timeline}
usa <- clean %>%
  filter(COUNTRY == "USA", lubridate::year(DATE) >= 2000)

ggplot(usa, aes(x = DATE, size = EQ_PRIMARY, colour = TOTAL_DEATHS)) +
  geom_timeline(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_timeline_label(aes(label = LOCATION_NAME), n_max = 5) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Richter scale value") +
  labs(colour = "# deaths") +
  theme_timeline()
```

```{r timeline-strata, fig.height = 5}
two <- clean %>%
  filter(COUNTRY %in% c("USA", "CHINA"), lubridate::year(DATE) >= 2000)

ggplot(two, aes(x = DATE, y = COUNTRY, size = EQ_PRIMARY, colour = TOTAL_DEATHS)) +
  geom_timeline(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_timeline_label(aes(label = LOCATION_NAME), n_max = 3) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Richter scale value") +
  labs(colour = "# deaths") +
  theme_timeline()
```

`geom_timeline_label()` takes `x` and `label` and labels the `n_max` largest
earthquakes (by the `size` aesthetic) of each time line.

## Map: `eq_map()` and `eq_create_label()`

`eq_map()` draws the epicentres on an interactive map; each circle has a radius
proportional to the magnitude and a pop-up with the column given in `annot_col`.

```{r map}
mexico <- clean %>%
  filter(COUNTRY == "MEXICO", lubridate::year(DATE) >= 2000)

eq_map(mexico, annot_col = "DATE")
```

`eq_create_label()` builds richer HTML labels (location, magnitude and total
deaths; missing values are left out):

```{r map-label}
mexico %>%
  mutate(popup_text = eq_create_label(.)) %>%
  eq_map(annot_col = "popup_text")
```
